name: Extended Schema Types for SEO – Proper Structured Data for Advanced SEO
author: Rede Piabanha

sections.description:
Build more complete structured data without abandoning the Yoast SEO interface or creating a second disconnected schema system.

Extended Schema Types for SEO – Proper Structured Data for Advanced SEO expands the native Yoast SEO > Schema selectors and enriches the connected JSON-LD graph already generated by Yoast SEO.

When an editor selects a specialized type, the plugin immediately displays the properties that WordPress and Yoast SEO cannot infer safely. Fields are separated into:

  • Required by Google: properties needed for the selected Google Search feature when they cannot be inferred.
  • Recommended by Google: properties documented by Google that can improve completeness and result quality.
  • Additional Schema.org fields: valid vocabulary that can help other consumers without being presented as a Google requirement.

Titles, canonical URLs, descriptions, featured images, authors, publishers and publication dates are reused from WordPress or Yoast SEO whenever that is reliable. The goal is to reduce duplicate entry while preventing incomplete objects from being presented as ready for Google.

Independent add-on disclaimer: this plugin is independently developed by Rede Piabanha. It is not developed, maintained, sponsored, endorsed or affiliated with Yoast BV or the Yoast SEO team. Yoast and Yoast SEO are trademarks of their respective owners.

Why install it?

  • Keep the familiar native Yoast SEO Schema workflow.
  • Avoid a second schema selector and disconnected JSON-LD output.
  • Use canonical CamelCase Schema.org names such as NewsArticle, WebApplication and DiscussionForumPosting.
  • Receive immediate required-property feedback while editing.
  • Enter only data that cannot be inferred safely.
  • Add connected entities to the Yoast SEO @graph instead of printing unrelated schema blocks.
  • Cover Google Search features as well as hundreds of additional Schema.org classes.
  • Keep all processing local to WordPress, with no external account, API key, tracking or remote data transfer.

Google Search property audit in version 1.1.0

Version 1.1.0 was reviewed against the current Google Search Central documentation. Google Search documentation is treated as authoritative for Google eligibility, while Schema.org remains the vocabulary reference.

The plugin validates required choices and conditional requirements, including:

  • mutually exclusive speakable.cssSelector and speakable.xpath;
  • isAccessibleForFree=false for marked paywalled sections;
  • physical, online and mixed event locations;
  • product snippet, merchant listing and product variant profiles;
  • Offer and AggregateOffer price/currency combinations;
  • shipping destination and delivery-time ranges;
  • return-policy alternatives and finite return windows;
  • aggregate rating count requirements;
  • nested review author and rating requirements;
  • software price 0 for free applications and aggregate rating or review;
  • Q&A answer counts and accepted or suggested answers;
  • recipe image, rating, nutrition and nested video requirements;
  • video live-broadcast and region restrictions;
  • job location or complete remote-job configuration;
  • image-license minimum metadata;
  • vacation-rental minimum image count and geographic data.

The plugin does not claim that markup guarantees a rich result. Google controls eligibility and presentation, and structured data must match visible page content.

Google Search feature coverage

The following profiles are represented directly or through nested properties in the connected graph.

  • Article / NewsArticle / BlogPosting: no extra mandatory Google property when Yoast SEO supplies the article basics; optional speakable and paywall data are conditionally validated.
  • Book actions: author, ISBN, book format, language, action target, platform, offer category and eligible region; purchase or rental actions also require price and currency. Book actions are a partner feature.
  • Breadcrumb: the existing Yoast SEO BreadcrumbList is preserved instead of duplicated.
  • Carousel / ItemList: ordered ListItem data, summary-page or single-page mode, and minimum item counts; Course lists require at least three courses.
  • Course: name is inferred from the post title and description is required; provider data is recommended.
  • Dataset: name is inferred and a 50–5,000 character description is required; distribution contentUrl becomes mandatory when a distribution is described.
  • Discussion forum: author, publication date and visible post content are generated or inferred; comments and interaction counts can be added with their own required properties.
  • Education Q&A: Quiz.hasPart flashcards with complete Question and accepted Answer data.
  • EmployerAggregateRating: reviewed organization, rating value and either rating count or review count.
  • ClaimReview: reviewed claim, rating object and textual rating; claim text length guidance is enforced.
  • Event: start date and a valid physical, virtual or mixed location; rescheduled events and offers are conditionally validated.
  • Image license metadata: image contentUrl plus at least one of creator, credit text, copyright notice or license; acquisition page is available as recommended data.
  • JobPosting: title, description and posting date are inferred; hiring organization and physical or fully remote location requirements are validated.
  • LocalBusiness: name is inferred and a physical postal address is required; specific LocalBusiness subtypes remain available.
  • MathSolver: SolveMathAction, target template, math-expression input, supported question type and learningResourceType=Math Solver.
  • Movie: name is inferred and image is required; director, creation date, ratings and reviews are available.
  • Organization: the base feature has recommended rather than mandatory properties; contact, identifiers, address, return policy, loyalty program and shipping policy can be added.
  • Product snippet: Offer, AggregateOffer, aggregate rating or review requirements are validated according to the selected profile.
  • Merchant listing: product image and a single Offer with price and currency are required; shipping and return-policy objects have conditional validation.
  • Product variants: ProductGroup, productGroupID, variesBy, single-page variants and multi-page canonical variant URLs are supported.
  • Loyalty program: MemberProgram name, description and tier benefits are validated when a program is entered.
  • Merchant return policy: either a merchant return link or country/category data; finite windows and return shipping fees have additional conditions.
  • Shipping policy: ShippingService and ShippingConditions with cost and/or delivery times, destination and order-value conditions.
  • ProfilePage: one Person or Organization main entity with its name inferred from the page title when possible.
  • QAPage: one Question with text, answer count and accepted or suggested answers.
  • Recipe: image is required; ingredients, instructions, times, yield, nutrition, rating and nested video fields are available and conditionally checked.
  • Review snippet: author, reviewed item and rating value are required for standalone Review; author length is limited to Google’s eligibility rule.
  • SoftwareApplication / WebApplication / MobileApplication: name is inferred, offer price is required (0 for free software), and aggregate rating or review is required; currency is recommended for paid apps.
  • Speakable: CSS selector or XPath can be supplied, but not both.
  • Paywalled content: marked sections require isAccessibleForFree=false.
  • VacationRental: identifier, occupancy, at least eight images and precise latitude/longitude are required. This is a limited-access Google feature.
  • VideoObject: name and upload date are inferred, thumbnail is required, and content URL, embed URL, clips, live broadcast and SeekToAction fields are available.

Some Google features are nested enhancements rather than independent page types. For example, loyalty, return and shipping policies belong under Organization or Product, while speakable and paywall properties belong on supported CreativeWork or Article markup.

Additional Schema.org coverage

The plugin also keeps hundreds of canonical Schema.org types available even when Google does not currently document a dedicated Search appearance for them. Those types receive safe generic Thing-level fields or a relevant specialized form.

Examples include HowTo, FAQPage, Service, Person, PodcastSeries, PodcastEpisode, AudioObject, MedicalEntity, Legislation, GovernmentService, DigitalDocument, WebApplication, MobileApplication and many more.

Availability in Schema.org does not imply current Google rich-result support. The editor clearly separates Google-required and Google-recommended data from additional Schema.org properties.

How it works

  1. Yoast SEO creates its normal connected JSON-LD graph.
  2. This plugin extends the native Page type and Article type option data.
  3. The selected type remains stored through the native Yoast SEO schema setting.
  4. Relevant fields appear immediately below the native selectors.
  5. Values are nonce-protected, capability-checked and sanitized before being saved as post metadata.
  6. The front end enriches the appropriate native graph piece or adds a connected entity linked to the Yoast SEO WebPage node.
  7. Empty properties and empty nested objects are removed before output.

Content and quality rules

Structured data must describe the primary visible content of the page. Do not add hidden, misleading, irrelevant or fabricated information.

Before publishing:

  • select the most specific accurate type;
  • complete every applicable field marked Required by Google;
  • add recommended fields only when the information is visible and accurate;
  • keep prices, availability, events, jobs, ratings, answers and policies synchronized with the page;
  • do not mark reviews or ratings controlled by the reviewed business when Google’s self-serving review restrictions apply;
  • validate the published URL with Google’s Rich Results Test;
  • inspect the rendered URL and monitor Search Console after deployment.

A valid result in a testing tool does not guarantee display in Google Search.

Privacy

The plugin operates locally. It does not call external APIs, create remote accounts, collect analytics or transmit post content to Rede Piabanha, Yoast or Google.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate Yoast SEO.
  2. Upload the plugin ZIP through Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin, or copy the extended-schema-types-for-seo directory to /wp-content/plugins/.
  3. Activate Extended Schema Types for SEO – Proper Structured Data for Advanced SEO.
  4. Edit a post, page or public custom post type.
  5. Open Yoast SEO > Schema.
  6. Choose the type that represents the page’s visible primary content.
  7. Complete the required and recommended fields shown below the native selectors.
  8. Publish or update the page and validate the public URL.
sections.faq:
Is this plugin made by Yoast?

No. It is an independent add-on developed by Rede Piabanha and is not affiliated with Yoast BV or the Yoast SEO team.

Does it require Yoast SEO?

Yes. The plugin extends the Yoast SEO Schema controls and connected JSON-LD graph. The WordPress.org dependency slug is wordpress-seo.

Does it create a second schema selector?

No. Additional types are inserted into the native Yoast SEO lists. Only the fields for the selected type appear below those lists.

Is NewsArticle included?

Yes. NewsArticle is explicitly available in the native Article type selector, together with descendants such as AnalysisNewsArticle, OpinionNewsArticle, ReportageNewsArticle and ReviewNewsArticle.

Is HowTo included?

Yes. HowTo remains available as valid Schema.org vocabulary with steps, supplies, tools, time and cost fields. Google does not currently list a dedicated HowTo appearance in the Search structured-data gallery.

Why are some required properties not shown as editable fields?

The plugin does not ask editors to re-enter properties that WordPress or Yoast SEO can infer reliably, such as the post title, canonical URL, author, publication date or featured image. The interface marks inferred requirements separately when applicable.

Why can a type be available without a Google profile?

Schema.org is broader than Google Search. The plugin offers extended vocabulary for other consumers while reserving Required by Google and Recommended by Google labels for documented Google Search features.

Does it guarantee rich results?

No. The plugin helps generate complete structured data, but Google controls eligibility and display. The visible page, site quality, policies and current Search support still apply.

Does it send data to another service?

No. All configuration and JSON-LD generation happen inside WordPress.

Which WordPress versions are supported?

Version 1.1.0 requires WordPress 6.5 or later and is tested through the WordPress 7.0 release line, including WordPress 7.0.2.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • Audited Google-supported structured-data profiles against current Google Search Central documentation.
  • Reclassified exposed properties as required, recommended or additional.
  • Added conditional validation for product snippets, merchant listings, variants, shipping, return policies and loyalty programs.
  • Added conditional validation for events, recipes, software applications, reviews, ratings, videos, Q&A, discussion posts and paywalled content.
  • Added additional author-type, review-count, region, return-policy, shipping-policy and organization fields.
  • Added nested forum comments and richer Q&A answer data.
  • Added field length and minimum-item constraints documented by Google.
  • Preserved native Yoast SEO selector integration and connected graph output.
  • Updated compatibility for WordPress 7.0 and PHP 7.4 or later.
  • Expanded commercial documentation, setup instructions and feature limitations.

1.0.0

  • Initial public release with native Yoast SEO selector integration and extended Schema.org type coverage.
